subject: Post-demo follow-up: observability & competitive comparison vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: observability & competitive comparison vs hyperscalers

Hi Alice — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary:
- Demo focused on per-route dashboards, trace capture (OTLP), and cost diagnostics.
- You asked for a side-by-side comparison vs the hyperscalers for observability surface (tracing format, retention, per-request latency breakdowns, and raw token-level cost breakdowns).

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a 48–72h POC):
1) Latency breakdown: run a 30m sustained set of requests (50 RPS peak, mixed prompt sizes) against Redwood hosted endpoint and your current hyperscaler endpoint. We'll collect per-request latency percentiles, token-level CPU/GPU breakdown, and KV-cache warm/cold metrics.
2) OTLP traces: we'll send OTLP spans (service.name=acme-llm) to your collector and provide example spans and attribute mappings so you can validate.
3) Dashboard parity: share a Drive doc with our dashboard snapshots and the minimal queries to reproduce (APM/Datadog/Grafana examples).

Attached: redwood-observability-overview.pdf (short deck), acme-mip-map.xlsx (internal mapping template).

Ask from you: confirm
- Which hyperscaler endpoint(s) you want us to compare against? (I heard AWS Bedrock + Hyperscale.ai — confirm)
- Access for a short-lived API key + preferred OTLP endpoint (host:port) so we can push traces to your collector during the POC.
- Any specific SLA/throughput targets we should hit for the test.

I'll schedule the POC kickoff once we have these. Aditya — looping you in on the test plan and load profile below. Stephanie — FYI on the procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: redwood-observability-overview.pdf, acme-mip-map.xlsx
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: observability & competitive comparison vs hyperscalers

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful. Confirming a few things: 

- Hyperscaler endpoints: yes, please compare against Bedrock (our current baseline) and Hyperscale.ai (we asked them for a trial yesterday; I've looped Tom).
- OTLP: we use OTLP/gRPC (collector at otlp.acme.internal:4317). We'll create a short-lived ingest token for the test window.
- SLA targets: 90th pctl latency < 300ms for small prompts (~128 tokens); 95th pctl < 800ms for mixed large prompts.

A couple asks from our infra/security side:
- Can you provide example trace spans and the mapping of Redwood attributes to our existing tracing schema? We need that before we open the collector port.
- Any PII handling guarantees during the POC (we prefer synthetic prompts where possible).

If you can share the runbook and trace examples, we can get procurement and infra to greenlight the short-lived key.

Best,
Alice Wong
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Corp
alice.wong@acme.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: observability & competitive comparison vs hyperscalers

Quick internal note with a recommended test plan (we'll use this to brief infra and SRE):

Test profile (to mirror Acme's expected workload):
- Duration: 45 minutes per provider (warm-up 10m + steady 30m + cooldown 5m).
- Traffic: mix of 50 RPS bursts; 5% chat-style multi-turn (KV cache exercised); 95% single-shot prompt mix (20–1024 tokens).
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (p0/p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU utilization, token generation time, KV cache hit/miss, memory spikes, OTLP span count and latencies.

Tracing & dashboards:
- We'll emit OTLP spans with the following tags: trace_id, span_id, model_name, model_variant, request_tokens_in, response_tokens_out, kv_cache_hit (boolean), batch_size, route_id.
- Provide sample span JSONs and a minimal Grafana dashboard (I'll drop links into the Drive doc).

Data handling:
- We'll use synthetic prompts by default for the POC. If Acme needs to test with redacted real prompts, we should run a short privacy review — recommend a 1h sync if so.

Next actions:
1) Marissa: share runbook + sample spans (I'll prepare the Grafana/Datadog queries).
2) Marissa/Alice: agree on test window and provide short-lived key + OTLP endpoint.
3) Aditya: spin up test harness and coordinate with SRE on the data retention for logs (we retain POC logs for 7 days by default).

I'll add this test profile to the HubSpot deal under RWIN-ACME-2026Q1.

- Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: observability & competitive comparison vs hyperscalers

Alice — thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a short runbook (redwood-obs-runbook.md) and two sample OTLP span JSONs. Below are the concrete next steps so we can schedule the POC kickoff: 

1) Acme to confirm test window (propose Wed 2026-03-11 09:00-11:00 PT) and provide short-lived key + OTLP endpoint (we need write access to otlp.acme.internal:4317 for the 2hr window).
2) Aditya will provision the test harness and post the Grafana/Datadog dashboards into the Drive doc.
3) Stephanie will follow up with procurement on the trial terms — if procurement needs a short MSA addendum for telemetry capture during the POC we can get legal involved.

Quoting here a small excerpt from the runbook (for quick review):
"During the POC we instrument request-level spans with model_name and kv_cache_hit. We provide a per-route dashboard that decomposes latency into: queuing, model execution (decode), and tokenization/serialization. We also publish token-level cost estimates per request so teams can compare unit economics vs baseline providers."

If that looks good, I'll schedule the kickoff and send a calendar invite after Alice confirms the window.

Thanks,
Marissa
